title: VECTOR: An Integrated Correlation Network Database for the Identification of CeRNA Axes in Uveal Melanoma
relevance_reason: The paper is about a biological database for RNA correlation networks in uveal melanoma; the name 'VECTOR' is an acronym (uVeal mElanoma Correlation NeTwORk) and has no connection to vector databases, vector indexing, or nearest neighbor search technology.
research_focus: Identification and visualization of competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory networks in uveal melanoma by integrating expression correlations, RNA-RNA interactions, sense-antisense overlapping data, and transcription factor binding data into a single interactive database.
method: Statistical elaboration of TCGA-derived expression data to compute correlation values among miRNAs, lncRNAs, and mRNAs, combined with predicted or validated RNA-RNA interactions, sense-antisense sequence overlapping data, and ChIPseq-based transcription factor binding data, all integrated into an interactive web-based database with graph visualization.
application_domain: Cancer genomics and RNA biology (uveal melanoma)
results_summary: The paper presents VECTOR, a web-based database that integrates TCGA-derived expression correlations among miRNAs, lncRNAs, and mRNAs with RNA-RNA interaction data, sense-antisense overlapping information, and transcription factor binding data for uveal melanoma. The database allows users to query by gene name and visualize ceRNA networks as interactive graphs with heatmaps. The authors validated their approach by confirming several network motifs (e.g., LINC00518/miR-199a-5p axis) and transcription factor regulations (e.g., CREB1, GABPA, SOX2) against existing literature. They also analyzed sense-antisense expression correlations, finding positive correlations most common in divergent pairs (over 80%) and negative correlations more frequent in convergent pairs (28.3% vs. 16.8%). The tool is presented as the most comprehensive integrated resource for RNA signaling in this rare intraocular cancer.
limitations: The UM TCGA dataset lacks physiological tissue data, preventing direct tumor-versus-normal comparisons; Stratification by clinicopathological features creates subgroups with low sample sizes, impairing statistical power; Multiple splicing variants of sense and antisense transcripts create a complex and heterogeneous scenario where no clear classification of overlapping regions was possible
research_gaps: The exact molecular mechanism underlying co-regulation or inverse correlation of sense and antisense transcripts is still under investigation; The VECTOR approach could be extended to build similar tools for other cancer models

title: Implementation and Evaluation of an Open-Source Chatbot for Patient Information Leaflets
